text:
Lucian Thorsen (COO): Hi. Thanks for hopping on. Short update.
Rep: Sure, Lucian. What's the news?
Lucian Thorsen (COO): We're going a different direction. I wanted to tell you myself.
Rep: Okay. Thank you for telling me. Can I ask what direction that is?
Lucian Thorsen (COO): We've decided to make a change. That's about all I can say right now.
Rep: Understood. Was there anything in the process that we could have done better?
Lucian Thorsen (COO): Not really. You've been great. The team has been great.
Delphine Abernethy (General Manager): Yes. I'll second that. Everyone we've dealt with at Lanternmere has been kind and professional. We really enjoyed meeting you all.
Rep: That is nice to hear. If you ever want to talk it through, even months from now, I'm around.
Lucian Thorsen (COO): Appreciate it. We'll keep that in mind.
Delphine Abernethy (General Manager): It was a good process. I mean that.
Rep: Thanks, Delphine. And thanks again for the time with the demo. I know you all carved out an afternoon.
Lucian Thorsen (COO): Sure. Of course. We'll stay in touch.
Rep: Sounds good. I'll send a short note after this.
Lucian Thorsen (COO): Great. Take care.
Delphine Abernethy (General Manager): Take care, and all the best to you.
Rep: You too. Bye.

Subject: Thank you

Hi,

Thank you for the call today, and for the time you and Delphine gave us over the last few weeks. We understand that you are going a different direction, and we respect that decision. Everyone on our team enjoyed working with you.

If anything changes in the future, or if you would like a conversation at any point, please reach out. Our door is always open, and we would be glad to hear from you.

Wishing you and the team at Redfern Fabrication all the best.

Warm regards,
Your Lanternmere HR rep

Hollis Vasquez (People Operations Lead): Let me walk you through the comparison we did, because I think it's useful to you.
Rep: I'd appreciate that.
Hollis Vasquez (People Operations Lead): Your quote: $52,800 for the year. Ninety-six people. That's $550 each. Tallyhold's quote: $36,000. $375 each. Same core modules, payroll, time, onboarding, benefits admin.
Rep: I see.
Hollis Abernethy (VP Finance): I was the one who reviewed the figures. Our approved budget for this category is $38,000. Their number fits. Yours doesn't. A $16,800 gap is not something I can absorb, not in a year where we are also renewing our lease.
Hollis Vasquez (People Operations Lead): And to be fair to you, I like your product better. The interface is cleaner. The reporting is better. I said that in the internal meeting. But I was outvoted, and the vote was about the number.
Rep: Would a reduced module set help?
Hollis Abernethy (VP Finance): We tried to model it. Dropping benefits admin got you to about $44,000. Still over.
Hollis Vasquez (People Operations Lead): So that's where we are. It's the number, no other reason.
Rep: Thank you for the clear explanation.

Subject: Decision on our evaluation

Hello,

Thank you for the thorough demonstration and the proposal. We have decided to go with Tallyhold. The comparison came down to cost: your annual quote was $52,800, about $550 per employee, and theirs came in at $36,000, or $375 per employee. Our approved budget for this category was $38,000, so only one of the two fit.

Please know that our team preferred your interface and reporting, and that this decision was made purely on cost. We appreciated your responsiveness.

Best regards,
Hollis Vasquez
People Operations Lead, Thornfield Design Studio

Bastian Oyelaran (VP of People): Hey, thanks for getting on. I wanted to talk through where things are, and I'm going to think out loud a little, bear with me.
Rep: Take your time.
Bastian Oyelaran (VP of People): So. You know we were all set. The demo went well, Bastian, my Bastian, the other one, the benefits one, was happy. We got the proposal. And then last Tuesday, our CEO announces we're, well, not a layoff, but a hiring freeze and a review of every vendor spend until, he said, the board meets in January. Which, okay, he's not wrong, but it kills this.
Rep: I'm sorry. That's a tough spot.
Bastian Oyelaran (VP of People): It is. And the awkward thing is, I'm kind of the sponsor of the whole project, and I'm also being told my own team might be restructured. So I can't even really champion it right now. If I'm honest, I might not even be here in March. I don't know. I'm just saying that out loud.
Bastian Cadogan (Benefits Manager): For what it's worth, I'd have signed it. The benefits setup looked right to me. I'd just be handing it off to nobody right now.
Bastian Oyelaran (VP of People): Right. So there's no other vendor. I want to be clear about that. We're not talking to anybody else, we're not unhappy with anything we saw. We're just stuck. We'll stay on our spreadsheets and our old payroll provider through the winter, seventy people, two states, it's manageable, painful, but manageable.
Rep: Would it be alright if I checked in after January?
Bastian Oyelaran (VP of People): Please do. Maybe by then I'll know who I'm reporting to. Ha. Yes, check in after the board meeting, I'd like that.
Bastian Cadogan (Benefits Manager): And keep the proposal handy. Don't let it go stale.

Annelise Ibarra (HR Director): Quick update. We're not signing. It's money.
Rep: Okay. Give me the numbers if you can.
Annelise Ibarra (HR Director): Your annual price lands around $44,000. Eighty-five people. About $520 each. Brasswick came back at $30,000. That's $350 or so. Our budget for the year is $32,000. Done.
Rep: Is there anything we could do on scope?
Annelise Ibarra (HR Director): I asked my CFO. He said no more than 32. Flat.
Priya Hollander (Compliance Lead): I'll say this. From a compliance angle, you were stronger. The audit trail, the I-9 handling, that was better. I wrote it up. It just wasn't enough to move a budget.
Annelise Ibarra (HR Director): Right. And, small thing, I was a little annoyed it took ten days to get the demo. I had momentum when I first called. But I'd have waited if the price worked. It's not why.
Rep: I understand. Can I ask if the Brasswick scope matches what we quoted?
Annelise Ibarra (HR Director): Close. We lose a few reports. I can live with that.
Priya Hollander (Compliance Lead): I'll miss the audit trail. But I'll live.
Annelise Ibarra (HR Director): So that's it. Thanks for being straight with us.
Rep: Thanks for telling me. If your budget cycle changes, call me.
Annelise Ibarra (HR Director): Will do.

Mirela Tillbrook (People Operations Lead): I'll skip the preamble. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Okay. Thank you for telling me directly. May I ask about the thinking?
Mirela Tillbrook (People Operations Lead): Our broker. We've used the same one for nine years. She runs our medical and dental renewals, she knows our claims history. Two weeks ago she came to us with a bundle, payroll and benefits admin together, from Tallyhold. She said, this is what I'd put you in. That was it, really.
Rep: Did she walk you through how it compared with what we showed you?
Mirela Tillbrook (People Operations Lead): She didn't have to. She gave us the package, priced, ready to sign. When your own broker says here's the answer, and she's the person you call at midnight in open enrollment, you listen.
Yuki Rourke (Operations Director): I'll second that. Three states, eighty-seven employees, and a renewal every autumn. Having her tied into the system means one less thing for me to chase.
Rep: Makes sense. Was there anything in our demo that fell short?
Mirela Tillbrook (People Operations Lead): No. Honestly, it was good. Six days from first call to demo, that was quick. Your team was professional. It's just that she's the one we trust with the money side of benefits.
Yuki Rourke (Operations Director): Our minds were mostly made up when we got her email, to be fair.
Rep: I appreciate your candor, both of you.
Mirela Tillbrook (People Operations Lead): Of course. Thanks for the time.

Oriel Okonkwo (VP of People): Straight up. We can't do it. Money.
Rep: Okay. What are we looking at?
Oriel Okonkwo (VP of People): You came in at $47,000 a year. We're seventy-three people. So about $640 each. Brasswick is at $33,000. That's $450. I don't have the extra fourteen. I just don't.
Rep: And the scope matches?
Oriel Okonkwo (VP of People): Close. They don't do as much on reporting. I'd take that trade. I'm tired, honestly. I have a budget and it's tight.
Beatrix Abernethy (Benefits Manager): For my part, your benefits admin is nicer. I'd have liked to use it. But I don't set the budget.
Oriel Okonkwo (VP of People): No. And the budget was set before any of this. $35,000, all in. Hard cap.
Rep: Could we phase the rollout to spread the cost?
Oriel Okonkwo (VP of People): We talked about it. The yearly number is the yearly number. Phasing doesn't change that.
Beatrix Abernethy (Benefits Manager): And, minor, it took eleven days to get the demo. That's a long wait for us. But it didn't decide this.
Oriel Okonkwo (VP of People): No, it didn't. It's the cost, it's just the cost. I'm sorry, I wish it were something more interesting.
Rep: It's okay. I appreciate you saying so.
Oriel Okonkwo (VP of People): Thanks for being decent about it.

Subject: Our decision, and thank you

Hi,

Thank you for the time and the demo. I wanted to put our decision in writing. We are going with Brasswick Payroll. Your yearly cost, about $47,000 or $640 per head for our 73 people, was well above the $35,000 we have available. Theirs is around $33,000. That is the reason.

Eleven days passed between our first call and the demo, which was longer than I wanted, but it did not decide anything. Beatrix liked your benefits tools.

Thank you again.

Oriel Okonkwo
VP of People, Larkspur Engineering

Mirela Abernethy (Chief People Officer): Keeping this short. We're moving ahead with Tallyhold.
Rep: Thanks for letting me know. Can you share what drove it?
Mirela Abernethy (Chief People Officer): Our broker. She's our benefits broker, been with us seven years, she handles every renewal. She brought us the Tallyhold bundle last week. Payroll and benefits together. She said, this is what I recommend. I take her recommendations seriously.
Rep: Was a comparison part of that?
Mirela Abernethy (Chief People Officer): Not really. It was the bundle she put in front of me. She had pricing, a timeline, the whole thing. I've learned that when she brings me a package like that, she's already done the homework.
Linnea Valdivia (Payroll Manager): From my side, I had no objections to what you showed. The payroll runs checked out. I tested the garnishment handling and it was right. I'd have been fine either way.
Mirela Abernethy (Chief People Officer): That's what makes this uncomfortable. It's not you. I just have eighty-one employees in one state, a small team, and a broker who handles the tedious benefits side for me. Taking her advice is the easy decision and, I think, the right one.
Rep: I understand. Is there anything we could do?
Mirela Abernethy (Chief People Officer): Honestly, no. If you were also a broker partner, we might be talking. But you aren't, as far as I know.
Rep: Fair. I appreciate your time.
Mirela Abernethy (Chief People Officer): Thank you. You were great.

Subject: Thank you for the evaluation

Hi,

Thank you for the demonstration and the follow-up. We have decided to move forward with Tallyhold. Our benefits broker has handled our renewals for years and recommended their bundle, and I am following her advice on this. It was a matter of trust in her judgment rather than any shortcoming in your product. Linnea was impressed with the payroll testing.

I appreciated your professionalism and responsiveness. If our situation changes, I will reach out.

Mirela Abernethy
Chief People Officer, Wexcombe Analytics

Rafferty Zeller (Office Manager): Hi. Got a few minutes. We decided.
Rep: Good to hear from you. What did you decide?
Rafferty Zeller (Office Manager): Tallyhold. I wanted to let you know before you heard from someone else.
Rep: Thanks. What made the difference?
Rafferty Zeller (Office Manager): Our broker. He does all our benefits renewals. Been doing them since before I started. He called me Thursday and said, I've got a bundle for you from Tallyhold. Payroll, benefits, it's all in one. He put the whole thing in front of me. I said, okay.
Rep: Did he compare it with what we showed?
Rafferty Zeller (Office Manager): Not that I recall. He just said it's what he'd go with. I trust him. He's got us through some bad renewal years.
Odalys Zeller (Payroll Manager): For what it's worth, I liked your payroll side. The time-off and PTO tracking was cleaner than I expected. But when the broker is the one handling the renewals and the contracts, it's easier to keep things with him.
Rafferty Zeller (Office Manager): Yeah. Seventy-seven people, two states, we don't have a huge team. One call to one guy is simpler.
Rep: I understand. Anything else I should know?
Rafferty Zeller (Office Manager): No. You were responsive. The demo was fine.
Rep: Thanks for letting me know directly.

Soren Petrakis (Office Manager): Good morning, and thank you for making time. I wanted to explain our decision, as I think you deserve that.
Rep: I appreciate it, Soren.
Soren Petrakis (Office Manager): We have decided to proceed with Tallyhold. It was a considerable deliberation, I must say.
Rep: May I ask what shaped it?
Soren Petrakis (Office Manager): Of course. Our benefits broker, who has handled our renewals for a number of years, recommended their package. She presented it to us as a bundle, payroll and benefits administration together, and she was quite confident about it. I have found her judgment sound in the past, and she manages all of the carrier relationships on our behalf. It seemed sensible to stay aligned with her.
Rep: Did she go through our proposal at all?
Soren Petrakis (Office Manager): I do not believe so. The bundle was what she put in front of us.
Dariusz Parekh (Payroll Manager): If I may. I thought your demonstration was careful and well organized. The demo was only a day after we first spoke, which I appreciated. I have no complaint about the payroll functionality.
Soren Petrakis (Office Manager): I would add one smaller point. The cost of the Tallyhold bundle was somewhat lower than your proposal, and that mattered to our owner. But I want to be clear that the broker's recommendation came first. With seventy-two employees across two states, we do rely on her.
Rep: I understand, and I thank you both for being so forthcoming.
Soren Petrakis (Office Manager): It was our pleasure. We wish you well.

Noor Fairweather (HR Generalist): Hi! Okay, so, I have to tell you, I feel bad, because I really liked you guys. But I might as well just say it, it came down to cost. I know, boring.
Rep: Not boring at all. Can you share the numbers?
Noor Fairweather (HR Generalist): Sure, so, your proposal was, um, around $50,000 for the year. We're eighty-four people. I did the math on a napkin, that's close to $600 each. Brasswick came in at about $34,000, so, what, $405 a person. And I know it's not the exact same thing, but it covers the big stuff, payroll, time clocks, onboarding.
Rep: Okay. And your budget?
Noor Fairweather (HR Generalist): Well, that's where Teodoro comes in. He's our finance director.
Teodoro Fonseca (Finance Director): Hello. Yes. We set aside $36,000 this year for the whole project. That's what the owner approved. Anything over, and I'd have to go back, and I wasn't going to win that argument. It's not a hundred percent your fault, a lot of software has gotten expensive, but there it is.
Noor Fairweather (HR Generalist): And I tried! I did. I said, but the demo, the way the PTO calendar works, my goodness, that was so much nicer. And he said, Noor, it's sixteen thousand dollars.
Teodoro Fonseca (Finance Director): I did say that.
Noor Fairweather (HR Generalist): So. I'm a bit sad. But that's the reality. If something changes, if you ever have a smaller package or a discount or something, I'd look again. I'd really be open to it.
Rep: That's kind of you. I will keep it in mind.
Noor Fairweather (HR Generalist): Please do. Thanks for everything, you were so patient with all my questions.

Nadia Okonkwo (Chief People Officer): I'll give you the answer and then the reason. The answer is no. The reason is price.
Rep: Okay. Help me understand the gap.
Nadia Okonkwo (Chief People Officer): Your annual comes to $55,000. We have eighty-six employees. That's about $640 per head. We got a quote from a competitor at $37,000. About $430 per head.
Rep: Were those comparable scopes?
Nadia Okonkwo (Chief People Officer): Roughly. We'd lose some of your analytics. We can live without it.
Kofi Hollander (Operations Director): From operations, I can say the platform looks good. Time clocks worked well in the trial. I'd have been comfortable with it. But I'm not the one holding the budget.
Nadia Okonkwo (Chief People Officer): The budget is $40,000. We had that number before we ever called you. I took it to the leadership team and said, can we go to fifty? They said no. I said, can we go to forty-five? No.
Rep: Would a longer term help?
Nadia Okonkwo (Chief People Officer): We looked. Even with a discount, it was $48,000. Short answer, the number doesn't fit.
Kofi Hollander (Operations Director): I'll say it plainly. It's not a quality problem. It's what we can afford.
Rep: Understood. Thank you both for being so clear.
Nadia Okonkwo (Chief People Officer): Thank you for your time.

Thaddeus Vasquez (Head of HR): Short version. Not this year. It's the price.
Rep: Walk me through it.
Thaddeus Vasquez (Head of HR): Your yearly number: $93,000. We're a hundred fifty-one people. That's about $616 each. Brasswick quoted around $62,000. About $410 each. My budget for the whole thing is $65,000.
Rep: And the Brasswick scope matches?
Thaddeus Vasquez (Head of HR): Mostly. They skip some reporting. Fine.
Jules Rourke (HR Director): I'll say, I preferred your interface. The employee self-service screens are better. But I have a limit, and so does Thaddeus.
Thaddeus Vasquez (Head of HR): Yeah. And there's one other thing, smaller. Our benefits broker has been pushing Tallyhold. She does our renewals. I can see where she's coming from, and I've told her I'd think about it. But that's not what moved me. It's the sixty-five versus ninety-three.
Rep: Could we discuss a phased approach to bring year one lower?
Thaddeus Vasquez (Head of HR): Even phased it's seventy-eight. Not under sixty-five.
Jules Rourke (HR Director): That's the number I saw too.
Thaddeus Vasquez (Head of HR): So it's a no for now. Appreciate the work.
Rep: Thank you. If your budget changes, please call.
Thaddeus Vasquez (Head of HR): Will do.

Mirela Galbraith (HR Generalist): Let me start with the data. We have 104 employees across four states, and our board gets a packet every quarter. I built the last one by hand. Eleven tabs. It took me nine working hours.
Rep: That's a lot.
Mirela Galbraith (HR Generalist): It is. And the premise of switching systems was to eliminate that. So I came to the demo with a list. Headcount by state by department, over time. Turnover rate by manager. Overtime hours as a percentage of regular. Cost per hire, by quarter. All sliceable.
Rep: What did you see when you tested those?
Mirela Galbraith (HR Generalist): Lucian can tell you, he was running it.
Lucian Abernethy (Payroll Manager): I tried to build all four. I got headcount by state. I could not get it by department too. I could not define a custom measure like overtime percentage. The fixed reports were clean, but I'd have to export everything to a spreadsheet and rebuild the packet. So we'd have the same nine hours.
Mirela Galbraith (HR Generalist): And that decided it. Your payroll was good. The multi-state tax handling looked right, which is a real worry at four states. The cost was in range. I told my director, if the reporting were flexible, I'd sign today. But it isn't.
Lucian Abernethy (Payroll Manager): The tax piece was fine. I want to be fair about that.
Mirela Galbraith (HR Generalist): So we're staying where we are while we look at something else. I'd be happy to look again if reporting changes. Do you have a sense of when?
Rep: I will find out and write to you.
Mirela Galbraith (HR Generalist): Please do.

Dariusz Fairweather (Office Manager): Hi. Honestly, I'm tired, so forgive me if I ramble. I wanted to close the loop.
Rep: No problem. What's the status?
Dariusz Fairweather (Office Manager): We're not moving forward. Not because of you. We're not picking anyone. We're just stopping.
Rep: Can you tell me what happened?
Dariusz Fairweather (Office Manager): Our owner sold a piece of the business. Which is a long story. But there's a new partner involved, and the first thing they did was freeze everything that isn't client work. Software, hires, even the office coffee. Seriously. So the project is stuck.
Maren Hollander (General Manager): I'll add, the person who was driving this, our old head of people, she left in September. I inherited it. I never had the context. And now I'm told to shelve it.
Dariusz Fairweather (Office Manager): That took a while, by the way. It was three weeks before we got to the demo. By then, things were already shifting. But I don't blame you. I blame, I don't know, the calendar.
Rep: Was there anything in the product you'd flag?
Dariusz Fairweather (Office Manager): No. The product was fine. The price was fine. If things were normal, I'd have said yes. We have a hundred fourteen people in five states and our current setup is held together with tape.
Maren Hollander (General Manager): I'd say reach out in the spring. Maybe by then we'll know who we answer to.
Rep: I will.
Dariusz Fairweather (Office Manager): Thanks. I'm sorry it's a non-answer.

Signe Petrakis (People Operations Lead): So, I'm tired, so let me be honest. We're not going with you. Not because of price, and not because of payroll. It's hiring.
Rep: Tell me more.
Signe Petrakis (People Operations Lead): We have a hundred thirty-four people, but we're growing. I posted twenty-two roles last quarter. I live in a spreadsheet for candidates. The whole idea was to get an applicant tracking piece in the same system as everything else. When I asked in the demo, you said, we integrate with a few outside tools. Which is fine, but then I'm paying for two products and syncing between them.
Rep: That's right, we don't have a native applicant tracking module.
Signe Petrakis (People Operations Lead): Right. And Ingrid, you saw this, too.
Ingrid Valdivia (IT Manager): I did. From the IT side, I'd be the one maintaining that integration. Four states, a hundred thirty-four employees, I don't want one more connector to babysit.
Signe Petrakis (People Operations Lead): The tax handling was good. Honestly it was. And the pricing, we could have lived with it. I know the demo only took three days to get on the calendar, and that was nice, I'll say that, but it doesn't matter.
Ingrid Valdivia (IT Manager): The thing that matters is the applicant tracking.
Signe Petrakis (People Operations Lead): So we're going with a platform that has it built in. I'm sorry. If you add it, I'd come back.
Rep: I will let you know.
Signe Petrakis (People Operations Lead): Please. Thanks for being understanding.

Lucian Abernethy (Head of HR): Okay. We're out. Here's why.
Rep: Please.
Lucian Abernethy (Head of HR): Eight days. First call to demo. Eight days. I called you on a Tuesday. I wanted a demo that week. I got one the next Wednesday.
Rep: I'm sorry. That's on us.
Lucian Abernethy (Head of HR): Here's what happened in those eight days. My COO got impatient. She said, we have a hundred eighty-five people and a payroll provider who's missing deadlines. We can't wait. So she told me to get a second vendor in. I did. Their person was on a call with us the next day.
Calla Jessamy (COO): I'll be direct. I don't wait. When something's broken, I want it fixed. We lined up another vendor while you were scheduling. By the time your demo came, we'd already done a kickoff.
Lucian Abernethy (Head of HR): Honestly, your demo was good. I told Calla that. I was a bit sad about it. But it was too late.
Rep: I understand. Is there any chance the other deal isn't final?
Calla Jessamy (COO): It's signed. We're past that.
Lucian Abernethy (Head of HR): It was the timing. It's not a product call. Next time, if there's a next time, move faster. That's all.
Rep: I'll take that to heart.
Lucian Abernethy (Head of HR): Good. Thanks for hearing me out.
Calla Jessamy (COO): Appreciate your time.

Odalys Delacroix (Head of HR): Oh, hi! Well, I'm glad I caught you. I'm sort of thinking out loud here, because I wanted to let you know in person. We're going a different direction.
Rep: Thank you for telling me directly. Can I ask what that looks like?
Odalys Delacroix (Head of HR): Um, I think the honest answer is that we're making a change. We've been thinking about it for a while. It's, you know, a lot of moving pieces.
Rep: I understand. Anything about our process you'd want us to know?
Odalys Delacroix (Head of HR): No, no, nothing like that. You were lovely. Everyone's been lovely. Sunniva, you were on the second call, you'd say the same, right?
Sunniva Hartigan (Benefits Manager): Oh, absolutely. Very kind, very professional. I enjoyed the demo.
Odalys Delacroix (Head of HR): See? It's really not about anything you did. I think we just landed somewhere. Different direction, that's the phrase, I keep coming back to it.
Rep: Totally fair. If it would help to talk it through later, I'm happy to.
Odalys Delacroix (Head of HR): That's kind. I'll keep it in mind. Maybe in a year, who knows?
Sunniva Hartigan (Benefits Manager): Stay in touch, though.
Rep: I will. And thank you both for your time.
Odalys Delacroix (Head of HR): Thank you. Oh, and say hi to the others on your team for me. Okay, I'll let you go. Bye now!

Idris Hollander (Office Manager): I'll keep it short, I'm beat. It's price.
Rep: Okay. Can you give me the numbers?
Idris Hollander (Office Manager): You quoted $71,000 a year. We're a hundred fifty-five people. So, about $458 each. Brasswick came in at $47,000. About $303 each. Our budget is $50,000. That's all there is.
Rep: Is the scope the same?
Idris Hollander (Office Manager): Close enough. They don't have as pretty a dashboard. I can live with that. I'm not here for pretty.
Lucian Santangelo (Operations Director): For what it's worth, I did like your scheduling tools. Hospitality has crazy shifts. But I don't own the budget.
Idris Hollander (Office Manager): No, I do, and it's $50,000. I asked for more. Got told no. Twice.
Rep: Could we get you closer with a reduced module set?
Idris Hollander (Office Manager): Tried that. Fifty-eight with the stripped-down version. Still over. So.
Lucian Santangelo (Operations Director): I wish it were different.
Idris Hollander (Office Manager): Yeah. It's just cost. Nothing else. Thanks for being decent about it.
Rep: Thank you. I appreciate the honesty.

Subject: Our decision

Hi,

Thanks for all the time. We are going with Brasswick. Your yearly price was about $71,000, which is close to $458 per person for 155 people. Theirs is $47,000. Our budget is $50,000, so I had no room. It was only about cost.

Lucian liked your scheduling tools. Thanks again.

Idris Hollander
Office Manager, Redfern Hospitality

Ravi Castellane (Chief People Officer): Tired, so I'll be plain. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Okay. Thanks for telling me. What was behind it?
Ravi Castellane (Chief People Officer): Our broker. She does all our benefits renewals. She came to me with a bundle, put it on the table, and said this is what she recommends. I trust her. She's been with us a long time.
Rep: Did she compare it to our proposal?
Ravi Castellane (Chief People Officer): Not really. She just brought the package. I didn't have the energy to argue. And frankly, I don't have the energy to run a second process.
Marisol Hollander (Finance Director): I'd add, from finance, the broker also handles the carrier negotiations. If that's all in one relationship, it's easier for me. I didn't dig into the numbers much, to be honest.
Ravi Castellane (Chief People Officer): And one small thing, to be fair. This project was already wobbling. We had a hiring freeze last quarter, and the owner has been wavering on all software. So it was likely to slip anyway. But the broker thing is what made it concrete.
Rep: I understand. Thank you both. With a hundred fifty-one people and three states, I know it's not a small decision.
Ravi Castellane (Chief People Officer): No. But it's made. Thanks for your time.

Subject: Thank you, and where we ended up

Hello,

Thank you for the demo and for your patience. We have decided to go with Tallyhold. Our benefits broker recommended their bundle, and since she handles our renewals and we trust her, we are following her advice. Our internal project had also slowed, so the timing worked out that way.

We appreciated your team's responsiveness and wish you well.

Ravi Castellane
Chief People Officer, Elmcroft Veterinary Partners

Yuki Parekh (Chief People Officer): Let me be efficient. We're going with Tallyhold. I wanted to tell you directly.
Rep: Thank you. Can I ask what led there?
